items_missed: No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — and this was the single clearest opening on the call. Kristin twice raised fragile items ('dishes and glasses that I would prefer not to break', 'a couple of mirrors'), and Lukas answered with packing technique instead of coverage. He then asked her to sign a plant waiver without ever telling her what IS covered.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — a first-time mover ('I have never paid for movers before') is the exact customer that pre-move-day email is designed to reassure.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned, even while booking a specific 8:39 AM start window.
No 'pricing is super simple' opener; jumped straight into packing-materials math when she asked what it costs.

What's-included never enumerated — he asserted 'our hourly rate is all inclusive' and listed what she WON'T be charged, but never named gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, or tools. The customer never learns what she's getting, only what she's escaping.

Save Your Ass speech was reactive, not delivered — the prep tips only came out because Kristin asked 'is there anything else I should know'. Framed as efficiency and mover safety, never as 'prep means a shorter move means a lower bill'.
'Take a carload' tip missing entirely — and she handed it to him, saying she'd move valuables herself in advance. That was the moment to say 'exactly, take a carload'.
Customer's name never used once in the call except when reading her email address back for typo-checking.
60c/lb baseline insurance never explained, so the plant waiver ask had no context.

Estimate variables incomplete — walk distance never discussed as a time factor despite parking distance changing between origin (0-20 ft) and destination (21-50 ft); additional stops never asked; number of trucks never stated.
Bolded-details list at the top of the confirmation email never previewed, and hours of operation never given ('reach out to us with this number' only).

Quoted the same job at four different numbers in sequence (999, then 666, then 666-888, then 777, then 888 with packing) while talking through his own math out loud. Kristin got there, but she had to work for it.
Transcript opens mid-probe, so greeting, name capture, 'how are you', and any agenda statement are not observable — Section 1 scored on captured audio only and may understate the open.
top_strength: The clock explanation was textbook and complete — clock starts when the crew arrives and does the walkthrough, two-and-a-half hour minimum, fifteen-minute increments after, 'you only pay for the time that gets used the day of' — all four beats in one clean pass. His probe was also genuinely thorough for a call this length: appliances, fragile and antique items, box count against a 25-35 benchmark for her home size, destination square footage, story count, and parking distance at both ends. Best moment was the recovery on the $682 website quote — instead of defending his higher number, he re-scoped to the smaller 600 sqft destination and walked the estimate down to a 666-888 range. That is a rep protecting estimate accuracy over a bigger-looking quote, and it is exactly the behavior that closes the 52% gap.
coaching_note: Lukas, the highest-leverage fix is No Worries Damage Coverage, and this call is the proof. Kristin told you twice she was worried about breaking things, and you gave her packing advice — then asked her to sign a waiver on her plants. She hung up not knowing Einstein covers up to $2,000 to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage. Say it the moment fragile items come up: 'And on that — every move includes our No Worries Damage Coverage, up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse anything we accidentally damage. So dishes and mirrors, you're covered.' That answers her actual question and makes the waiver land as a plant-specific exception instead of a red flag. Second priority: you gave the prep advice but never attached it to money. You said 'the more prepared you are the more efficient we can be' — finish the thought with 'and since you only pay for the time we use, every box you have packed and every drawer you empty comes straight off your bill. Anything small and fragile, take a carload over yourself — she already told you she planned to. Does that make sense?' Third, use her name. You never said 'Kristin' once on a fifteen-minute call where she ended by telling you that you made a move that sucks way better — you had the rapport, you just left the easiest three points on the table.
phone_presence_notes: The Donatello plant story landed real rapport and Kristin closed with 'moving sucks and you're making it way better', but the language rambles and self-corrects heavily and he never once used her name.
